subject: sociology
topicName: The Role of the Family in Society

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Functionalist view: the family serves essential functions for society. Murdock (1949): the nuclear family is universal and performs four functions - sexual (regulates sexual behaviour), reproductive (produces next generation), economic (pools resources), educational (socialises children). Parsons: the family serves two 'irreducible' functions - primary socialisation of children and stabilisation of adult personalities (warm bath theory).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Marxist view: the family serves capitalism, not society as a whole. Zaretsky (1976): the family consumes capitalist products (TVs, cars, processed food) and provides unpaid domestic labour (women's housework reproduces the next generation of workers at no cost to the state). The family is a 'unit of consumption' and an 'ideological conditioning device' that supports capitalism.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Feminist view: the family is patriarchal and oppresses women. Delphy and Leonard: women do most unpaid domestic labour, enabling men to work while the family benefits men economically. Radical feminists: the family is the root of patriarchy - domestic violence, sexual violence and emotional abuse are normalised within families. Firestone: the family must be abolished to achieve gender equality.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Interactionist view: the family is created through everyday interactions. Berger and Kellner: marriage involves a 'negotiated reality' where couples construct shared meanings and roles through daily interaction. The family is not a fixed structure but an ongoing accomplishment.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Compare Functionalist and Marxist views of the role of the family. | Evaluate the Feminist view that the family oppresses women. | Assess which perspective provides the most useful understanding of the family in modern society.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Functionalism: family benefits EVERYONE (functions). Marxism: family benefits CAPITALISM (exploitation). Feminism: family benefits MEN (patriarchy). Murdock: 4 functions (sexual, reproductive, economic, educational). Parsons: 2 functions (socialisation, stabilisation). Zaretsky: family = unit of consumption. Delphy & Leonard: family = patriarchal exploitation. Smart: ask people what family means to THEM.
